new_statements.quote: 4.3.1.1 Syllabics (vowels). Vowels in Laria cannot be contrasted for length. Vowel lengthening is used for emphasis or stress. [...] 4.3.2 STRESS. Stress has no role in the language except when used for emphasis. 4.3.3 PITCH. Pitch is not distinctive in the language. There are no forms distinguished from others purely by pitch.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The author treats stress as non-distinctive and gives it no word-level function or fixed position; stress (with vowel lengthening and a raised intonation peak) is described only as a sentence-level device for emphatic and contrastive focus (4.3.4.2-4.3.4.3). No default stressed syllable is identified.
new_statements.exceptions: None; only emphatic/contrastive sentence stress is described (higher-than-average intonation peak on the emphasised constituent).
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns the word/lexical level (no role) versus utterance-level emphasis. The variety described is 'Laria', the in-group Chhattisgarhi of the Agharia caste in Sundargarh/Jharsuguda/Sambalpur (western Odisha) and Raigarh, a receding contact variety under heavy Sambalpuri/Oriya influence; data from 10 villages, 2 towns, 2 cities (ch. 1.5). For Standard (Raipur-Bilaspur) Chhattisgarhi the only information found is second-hand: Varma 1995 reports that N. D. Verma 1979 posits 'anumeya' (predictable) vs 'sarthak' (significant) balaghat and that Shankar Shesh 1973 sees accent operating at sentence level - the actual placement rule in Verma 1979 (pp. 139-148) was not accessible.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted first-hand statement describes 'Laria' = the home variety of Chhattisgarhi spoken by the Agharia caste in western Odisha (Sundargarh, Jharsuguda, Sambalpur) and adjacent Raigarh, an obsolescing contact variety under strong Sambalpuri/Oriya influence (Naik 1999). 'Laria/Lariya' is listed by LSI, Masica and Ethnologue as an alternative (eastern) name of Chhattisgarhi [hne, chha1249] and has no separate glottocode, but People of India and the Raigarh Gazetteer treat it as a distinct mixed sub-dialect; it is not Standard (Raipur-Bilaspur 'Kendri') Chhattisgarhi. The only information located for the standard variety is second-hand (Varma 1995 summarising N. D. Verma 1979 and Shankar Shesh 1973). Note also Shodhganga records the thesis author as 'Maik, Ajit Kumar' but the title page reads 'Ajit Kumar Naik'.

sources.citation: Devi, Sushila (1987). A Historical and Comparative Study of Eastern Hindi Phonology. PhD thesis, Dept. of Linguistics, Banaras Hindu University. Shodhganga hdl 10603/534910.
sources.note: Diachronic (OIA > Awadhi/Bagheli/Chhattisgarhi); invokes accent only historically ('pre-accented vowels lost', 'final vowels suffered due to lack of stress'); no synchronic statement of where stress falls in Chhattisgarhi.

sources.citation: Kavyopadhyaya, Hira Lal; translated by G. A. Grierson; revised and enlarged by Lochan Prasad Kavya-Vinod (1921). A Grammar of the Chhattisgarhi Dialect of Eastern Hindi. Calcutta: Baptist Mission Press (ix+225 pp.). DLI scan on archive.org (in.ernet.dli.2015.279313).
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: WID Old Widener 3254.59.25; FIG HathiTrust (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Nothing on accent/stress anywhere (full-text grep for accent/stress/emphasis/syllable checked and the Alphabet/Vowels/Consonants/Phonetical-changes chapter read). Only prosodically relevant statement is a quantity rule, p. 23: 'When in a tadbhawa word a long vowel, owing to inflection, conjugation or other cause, finds itself in the antepenultimate or other earlier syllable, that vowel is shortened' (ama -> am'wa, ghora -> ghor'wa); also describes the 'neutral or imperfect vowel' (ghar', ghor'wa) after Hoernle.

sources.citation: Kar, Chittaranjan & Sudhir Sharma (eds.) (2000). Chhattisgarhi bhasha: svarup aur sambhavnaen [in Hindi]. (archive.org chhattisgarhi-bhasha-2000)
sources.note: Brief 'dhvani-prakriya' section: 5 short + 5 long vowels, nasalization, extra length distinguishes jaithaun/jathaun, 35 consonants, gemination; nothing on stress. Cites Narendra Dev Verma 1979:27.

sources.citation: Varma, Poonam (1995). Manak Chhattisgarhi shabdon ka arthparak adhyayan [A semantic study of Standard Chhattisgarhi words; in Hindi]. PhD thesis, Dept. of Linguistics, Pt. Ravishankar Shukla University, Raipur. Shodhganga hdl 10603/30967.
sources.note: Second-hand only (pp. 11-12, 16; image PDF read visually): summarises earlier Hindi descriptions - Shankar Shesh 1973: 'ekakshari, dvi-akshari aur tin akshar vale shabdon men kisi vishesh arth ke dyotan ke lie svaraghat ka prayog vakya star par dikhai padta hai' (accent appears at sentence level to signal special meaning); Narendra Dev Verma 1979: 'balaghat - ise do bhagon men vibhakt kiya gaya hai - (1) anumeya balaghat, (2) sarthak balaghat' (stress: predictable vs. significant). Author concludes (p. 16) Standard Chhattisgarhi has 'sandhij 5, balaghat 2, surtan 3' but says determining them…
